meta.title: Siaya County: ten-year fiscal history
meta.unit: KSh billion unless stated; revenue and pending bills in KSh million
meta.basis: Nominal (money of the day). Fiscal year runs 1 July to 30 June.
meta.note: Each year is read from the Controller of Budget annual county report for that year. Where two reports give different values for the same year, both are kept in 'alternates'.
gaps: FY2013/14: approved budget and pending bills not shown (only spending, absorption and revenue quoted in the FY2014/15 report). FY2014/15: pending recurrent bills were not reported.

FY2019/20: Controller of Budget report not found. The annual county report for this year is not in the Parliament library and cob.go.ke was unreachable (21 Nov 2026; searched again 27 Nov 2026), so the series has no approved budget, recurrent/development split, spending, absorption, own-source revenue target or pending bills for it. Own-source revenue (KSh 179.43m) comes from the FY2020/21 report. The county's Budget Review and Outlook Paper (budget by part, spending, absorption, own-source revenue and its target), the FY2020/21 report's look-back figures (own-source revenue, development spending of KSh 2.12bn, balance brought forward, statutory deductions) and the Senate figures are listed under supplementary and on /counties/siaya/ledger/ (fiscal reconciliation); they are not used in the series. Where they disagree (own-source revenue 184.25 against 179.43; development spending 2,155.01 against 2,120) both values are in the conflict register.

Audit opinions for FY2016/17 to FY2018/19: the Auditor-General's own reports are still not held. The opinions shown come from the Parliamentary Budget Office's County Fact Sheets 2024, an official compilation (secondary), as explained under audits.

FY2025/26: the full year is read from Part 1 of the Controller of Budget annual county report for FY2025/26 (August 2026), whose chapter 2 tables give every county's budget, spending, absorption, own-source revenue and trade payables (scanned; read by OCR twice). Part 2, which holds the Siaya chapter (its narrative, department tables and wage-bill ratio), is not in the Parliament library, so those details remain a gap. The in-year reports (first quarter and first half) stay under in_year as partial-year figures and are not compared with the full year.
meta.pending_rule: Pending bills in years: the closing stock as printed in that year's own Controller of Budget report (own-year rule, sweep D5, 21 Nov 2026). A stock for the same date in another report is listed in the conflict register, and years with an open ledger discrepancy are marked on the pages.

audits.label: Auditor-General opinion on the County Executive of Siaya's accounts
audits.note: Opinions for FY2014/15 and FY2015/16 come from a Senate committee compilation of Auditor-General opinions (annexes to the Senate fiduciary risk report, November 2018), not from the audit reports themselves, so they are graded lower; the FY2014/15 opinion may cover the County Executive and County Assembly together. Opinions for FY2016/17 to FY2018/19 come from the Parliamentary Budget Office's County Fact Sheets 2024 (April 2025), an official compilation (secondary), because the Parliament library holds no County Executive of Siaya audit report for those years and the Auditor-General's site still serves a bot check (27 Nov 2026); they are graded lower still, and the PBO table gives the opinion only. For FY2016/17 the civil-society Chambua summary (National Taxpayers Association) prints the same opinion; it is listed as corroboration, not as a source. FY2019/20 comes from a Senate committee report that quotes the audit, so it is graded lower. The first entry covers 16 months, not a full fiscal year, and the whole county government (executive and assembly together); the later entries cover the County Executive only.
